He played college basketball for [[Michigan State University]].{{cite news |author1=Adam Biggers |title=Kalin Lucas' legacy at Michigan State is in serious jeopardy |url=https://www.mlive.com/spartans/2011/02/kalin_lucas_legacy_at_michigan.html |access-date=23 August 2022 |work=[[The Flint Journal]] |publisher=[[Michigan Live]] |date=9 February 2011}}{{cite news |author1=Mike Defabo |title=Ex-MSU star Kalin Lucas 'one step closer' to NBA dream - still thinks of MSU days, regrets |url=https://eu.lansingstatejournal.com/story/sports/college/msu/mens-basketball/2019/02/27/michigan-state-basketball-kalin-lucas-one-step-closer-nba-dream/3003162002/ |access-date=23 August 2022 |work=[[Lansing State Journal]] |date=27 February 2019}} ==High school career== Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Lucas was listed as the No. 6 point guard and the No. 38 player in the nation in 2007.[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Kalin-Lucas-41701;_ylt=Auzea0roXp6YFV9d0yxtCCBGPZB4 Kalin Lucas Recruiting Profile] ==College career== As a freshman, Lucas immediately saw heavy playing time for the 2007–08 [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Spartans]], averaging 25.1 minutes per game.{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Kalin-Lucas/Summary/2313|title=Kalin Lucas Player Profile|work=RealGM.com|access-date=September 17, 2014}} His team-leading 13.5 points per game in the first two rounds of the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]] were a major component of their [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|Sweet Sixteen]] run.{{cite web|url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032508aab.html|title=Michigan State Makes Seventh Trip To Sweet 16 In Last 11 Seasons|work=msuspartans.com|date=March 25, 2008|access-date=September 17, 2014|archive-date=July 10, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140710191209/http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032508aab.html|url-status=dead}} During his sophomore season, Lucas earned Big Ten Player of the Year honors, All-Big Ten first-team selection, and was named Michigan State's MVP, all while carrying the Spartans to the National Championship game against North Carolina. He led MSU in scoring (14.7 ppg), field goals made (173) and attempted (438), free throws made (172) and attempted (213), assists (4.6 apg) and minutes (31.9 mpg), while ranking second in steals (39).{{Cite web|url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/lucas_kalin00.html|title=Kalin Lucas Bio|access-date=May 18, 2011|archive-date=September 7, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150907013513/http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/lucas_kalin00.html|url-status=dead}} Lucas continued to lead the Spartans in his junior season, as he earned All-Big Ten first-team honors and was also named Co-MVP of the team, along with Raymar Morgan. On January 26, 2010, he made a mid-range jumper at Michigan with 3.5 seconds remaining, which gave Michigan State a one-point lead, and eventually a 57–56 victory over their in-state rivals. He struggled to stay healthy the rest of the season, spraining his ankle a month before the Big Ten Tournament and eventually rupturing his Achilles tendon in the second round of the 2010 NCAA Tournament against Maryland. Lucas' season was instantly put to an end, but the Spartans rallied, making their way to a second straight Final Four appearance. Lucas was voted Team MVP and All-Big Ten second team during his senior season. He finished his four-year career at Michigan State as the school's all-time leader in free-throws made (507) and attempted (637). He is also one of just four Spartans to total 1,500 career points and 500 career assists, finishing his career with 1,996 total points. ==Professional career== ===2011–2015=== On July 23, 2011, Lucas
